claims.text: A heat treatment that produces incoherent or semi-coherent nanoprecipitates will significantly increase the coercive field of a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
The proposed effect applies to a CoFeNiTaAl-based high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy normally exhibits soft-magnetic behavior with low coercivity.
The initial state is as-cast or homogenized.
A tailored annealing and cooling schedule can preferentially produce incoherent or semi-coherent rather than fully coherent nanoprecipitates.
Incoherent or semi-coherent nanoprecipitates act as strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Fully coherent nanoprecipitates only minimally disturb magnetic domain walls.
Incoherent precipitates generate local lattice distortions.
The distortions and magnetic inhomogeneities created by incoherent precipitates pin domain walls more effectively than coherent precipitates do.
More effective hindrance of domain-wall motion results in increased coercive field.
Coherent and ordered nanoprecipitates in the cited CoFeNiTaAl alloy increase coercivity only marginally, to less than 10.7 Oe.
The modified sample will have a quantifiably higher coercive field than an otherwise matched precipitate-free or coherent-precipitate control.
The hypothesized effect should hold when precipitate sizes remain below approximately 15 nm.
Holding composition, treatment duration, and other variables constant allows coercivity differences to be attributed solely to precipitate coherency.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that only precipitate coherency is altered, but the allowed control may be precipitate-free. Comparing an incoherent-precipitate sample with a precipitate-free sample changes precipitate presence, volume fraction, and potentially size distribution in addition to coherency, so the effect cannot be attributed solely to coherency.
